sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 1975. Études yakoma, langue du groupe oubanguien (R.C.A.): morphologie, synthématique. (Bibliothèque de la SELAF 47-48.) Paris: SELAF. Ch. II 'Révision phonologique', pp. 17-26 only (Rosetta Project excerpt).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, HathiTrust search-only
sources.note: Yakoma [yky], the variety Ethnologue says Dendi has 'high intelligibility' with. Revision of the author's 1973 phonology: phoneme status of n/l/r, utterance-level vowel and tone rules, B/M/H tones with contours. a full-text search for stress/accent|intensit|tonique|dendi = 0 hits; silent on stress. Same excerpt is the deciding source already held for yako1252.

sources.citation: Roulon-Doko, Paulette. 2020. Introduction sur les langues oubanguiennes. ILARA lecture slides (HAL halshs-03075359).
sources.note: Gbaya-centred overview; 'Langue à tons (schèmes lexicaux..)'; nothing on Dendi, Ngbandi prosody, or stress.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2014. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 17th ed., entry Dendi [deq]. Dallas: SIL International. (the Internet Archive 2014-10-09.)
sources.note: 'Population 10,000 (1996). Location Mbomou Prefecture, Gambo-Ouango subprefecture.. Classification Niger-Congo.. Ubangi, Ngbandi. Dialects None known. High intelligibility of Yakoma [yky]. Ngbandi [ngb] and Mbangi [mgn] may be inherently intelligible of Dendi.. Writing Unwritten. Other Comments Different from Dendi [ddn] in Benin and Nigeria.' No phonology.

sources.citation: Hartell, Rhonda L. (ed.). 1993. Alphabets of Africa. Dakar: UNESCO/SIL. Ngbandi (Zaire) orthography page (Rosetta Project scan).
sources.note: Phoneme/orthography chart only; nothing on tone marking or stress.

sources.citation: Kamanda Kola. 1989. La conjugaison en ngbandi (langue non bantu). Annales Aequatoria 10: 181-199.
sources.note: Ngbandi of the Yakoma collectivity (Zaire), i.e. a sister variety. p. 182: 'Cette langue compte une dizaine de dialectes (3)'; n. 3 (p. 198): 'Ce sont : bwato, yakoma, abasango, sango, mbati, ngiri, bangi, dendi.' sec. 1.2 'Phonèmes suprasegmentaux' (pp. 183-184): 'Le ngbandi distingue trois tonèmes simples et deux tonèmes complexes' (bas, moyen, haut; descendant HB/HM, montant BH/BM) plus a 'durème' = intonational vowel length at word/phrase edge for insistence/interrogation. No mention of accent or stress anywhere in the article (the 'accent' hits in the volume belong to other articles on C…

sources.citation: Boyd, Raymond. 1988. Le kpatiri ou gbayi, une nouvelle langue du groupe ngbandi. In Yves Moñino (ed.), Lexique comparatif des langues oubanguiennes, 35-49. Paris: Geuthner. (HAL hal-00344525, author's annotated version.)
sources.note: Ngbandi-group comparison (gbayi vs yakoma, sango, ngbandi): tone classes H/M/B and HB contours in nouns and verbs (secs 11-17); no mention of Dendi and no mention of accent/stress.

sources.citation: Tucker, A. N. & M. A. Bryan. 1966. Linguistic Analyses: The Non-Bantu Languages of North-Eastern Africa. London: OUP for IAI. Ch. 'The Banda-Gbaya-Ngbandi languages', sec. 2 'Tone and Stress' (Google Books page scan of the 2017 Routledge reprint, PT92).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number 2235.4.26; Linguistics Library, call number CoPh 36.88)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number 2235.4.26; Linguistics Library, call number CoPh 36.88
sources.note: Group-level: '2a. There appear to be three main tone levels in these languages--High, Mid, and Low.. Lekens further records a vowel-less tone.. in NGBANDI'; '2b. Stress is often responsible for changes in vowel quality and vowel length. In MAYOGO.. In NGBAKA, GBAYA, and BANDA..' -- no stress statement for NGBANDI and Dendi is not named.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (fr), 'Ngbandi (langue)' and 'Dendi (République centrafricaine)'; Wikipedia (en) 'Ngbandi language' (raw wikitext).
sources.note: fr: 'Pour Boyeldieu, le ngbandi, yakoma, le sango, le dendi et le mbangi forment une même langue' (citing Boyeldieu 1975: 16; Boyeldieu & Diki-Kidiri 1982: 16). Bibliography adds Lekens 1952 Dictionnaire ngbandi (Tervuren) and Moñino 1988. Nothing on stress.
